summary: Ledger-first: the hash-chained JSONL ledger is the only source of truth; decisions, constraints and questions are projected into a rebuildable SQLite index. Graphiti is optional asynchronous enrichment, never on the write path.

record.text: Ledger-first: the hash-chained JSONL ledger is the only source of truth; decisions, constraints and questions are projected into a rebuildable SQLite index. Graphiti is optional asynchronous enrichment, never on the write path.
record.rationale: Verified 2026-10-21: the LLM gateway has no embeddings endpoint, GLM 5.3 always reasons (6-12s/call, so ~1-2 min per Graphiti write), and LLM extraction turns structured decisions into lossy entity-fact triples with non-deterministic supersession. Lenses already write structured records, so store them as such.

summary: Keep any LLM provider pluggable; don't hard-wire the LLM gateway.

record.text: Keep any LLM provider pluggable; don't hard-wire the LLM gateway.
record.rationale: Whether nazareth is a work or personal project is undecided, and the LLM gateway is a work resource.

summary: The MCP server is host-agnostic. Ship Claude Code lenses first; Docker Agent lenses second.

record.text: The MCP server is host-agnostic. Ship Claude Code lenses first; Docker Agent lenses second.
record.rationale: Claude Code is where daily work happens, so it gives the fastest honest signal on whether memory reduces drift. Docker Agent's routing hooks and sandbox are layers on top, not the foundation.

summary: Dogfood on nazareth itself first. Firefly later, with .nazareth/ gitignored and lenses limited to reading and logging at first.

record.text: Dogfood on nazareth itself first. Firefly later, with .nazareth/ gitignored and lenses limited to reading and logging at first.
record.rationale: Firefly has existing users; nazareth must prove itself on a project where a misbehaving lens costs nothing.
Keeps decision history with the code. A hash chain can't be merged across branches, which is acceptable because this is a single-branch project.

summary: Order after the core: Claude Code lenses + dogfooding, then semantic search (LanceDB + local embeddings), then Docker Agent lenses and routing, then optional Graphiti.

record.text: Order after the core: Claude Code lenses + dogfooding, then semantic search (LanceDB + local embeddings), then Docker Agent lenses and routing, then optional Graphiti.
record.rationale: Dogfooding shows whether FTS keyword search is enough before investing in embeddings.

summary: No LLM or network calls on the write path. Embeddings, Graphiti and other enrichment are derived from the ledger asynchronously and must be rebuildable.

record.text: No LLM or network calls on the write path. Embeddings, Graphiti and other enrichment are derived from the ledger asynchronously and must be rebuildable.
record.rationale: Writes stay deterministic and take milliseconds; enrichment models can be swapped and re-indexed from the ledger.

summary: A record supersedes another only by naming its id, and only if that record is active (otherwise the error names the current one). A same-topic decision that doesn't supersede the active one, or a lens superseding a human decision, is recorded as pending for the human. Policy outcomes are stored in the event so replay is faithful.

record.text: A record supersedes another only by naming its id, and only if that record is active (otherwise the error names the current one). A same-topic decision that doesn't supersede the active one, or a lens superseding a human decision, is recorded as pending for the human. Policy outcomes are stored in the event so replay is faithful.
record.rationale: Turns silent drift into either an explicit, reasoned change or a visible item for the human.

summary: Each lens runs its own nazareth server process. Ledger appends take an exclusive flock and re-read the chain head; check-then-write logic runs inside ledger.transaction() after index.sync().

record.text: Each lens runs its own nazareth server process. Ledger appends take an exclusive flock and re-read the chain head; check-then-write logic runs inside ledger.transaction() after index.sync().
record.rationale: Without this, concurrent writers forked the chain (reproduced with a 4-process test against the original code).

summary: Project state lives in .nazareth/ and nothing is created until the human runs `nazareth init`; derived files are gitignored inside it.

record.text: Project state lives in .nazareth/ and nothing is created until the human runs `nazareth init`; derived files are gitignored inside it.
record.rationale: Pointing a lens or MCP config at an unrelated repo must never create state there by accident.

summary: Target the MCP Python SDK 2.x (MCPServer); agent-facing failures raise NazarethError, converted to ToolError so the message reaches the agent.

record.text: Target the MCP Python SDK 2.x (MCPServer); agent-facing failures raise NazarethError, converted to ToolError so the message reaches the agent.
record.rationale: 2.3 is installed and FastMCP no longer exists; generic exceptions reach agents only as 'Error executing tool'.

summary: Only state changes are written to the ledger; read-only tool calls are not logged.

record.text: Only state changes are written to the ledger; read-only tool calls are not logged.
record.rationale: Logging reads would bury the history that matters. This deliberately departs from the original 'all MCP calls are self-audited' design.

summary: Each Claude Code lens subagent defines its own inline nazareth MCP server with a fixed NAZARETH_ACTOR and denies the main session's nazareth tools.

record.text: Each Claude Code lens subagent defines its own inline nazareth MCP server with a fixed NAZARETH_ACTOR and denies the main session's nazareth tools.
record.rationale: Identity is set by config rather than trusted to the model. Verified: inline servers load only in trusted folders, and without the deny rule a lens silently falls back to the parent server's identity.
